spine: 1. 反直覺觀察：首月 140 名工程師登入新 IDP，第三月剩 28 個（且多是平台團隊自己人），八成工程師三個月內默默棄用、走回複製貼上 Dockerfile 的老路。
2. 排除假說一（UI 不夠好）：平台有主題化 UI、自訂 plugin、VP mandate，介面品質不是死因——UI 越漂亮，期待落差反而越傷人。
3. 假說二（YAML 維護稅是驅離的症狀）：catalog-info.yaml 要手寫、跨 12 repo 維護、owner 打錯字 parser 靜默失敗、兩週後才發現；工程師拒絕為『不看的 dashboard 上一個漂亮 icon』花 20 分鐘 debug YAML。
4. 症狀不是病因：填完 YAML 換來的報酬是零，因為底層苦工一步沒少——這把調查引向更下面一層。
5. 根源：Backstage 是 portal 不是 platform——立起了一片玻璃（pane of glass），卻沒蓋玻璃後面的 provisioning engine；點 Create New Service 只拿到空 repo＋壞掉的 CI＋一張 Jira ticket。
6. 工程師真正要的：不是 UI，是能用的 CLI——他們住在 terminal 與 IDE 裡，想跑一行指令並讓它真的成功。
7. 修法三規則（paved road 非收費站／自動化優先 UI 其次／state 用發現不用宣告，Humans drift; discovered state does not），轉向後 time-to-first-deployment 從三週降到 12 分鐘。

perspective.mechanism: IDP 的設計本質：portal（一片聚合資訊的 UI 玻璃）vs platform（底層真正 provision infra、管理 state、執行 policy 的引擎）。Backstage 提供的是 portal，團隊誤把它當 platform，蓋了玻璃沒蓋引擎。
perspective.tradeoff: 團隊用一層漂亮的 React 前端 + metadata catalog，換掉了『真正自動化底層 provisioning』的工作——把平台維護成本（catalog-info.yaml）轉嫁給使用者，卻沒給出等值回報（服務並沒有被自動 provision）。
perspective.reader_use: 台灣工程 lead 評估自建 IDP／導入 Backstage 時的驗收問題：拿掉 UI，底層能不能一行 CLI 端到端 provision 出服務並真的成功？不能就是 portal 不是 platform。並警惕『要使用者手寫 metadata schema』這種收費站設計。

notes.quote: In month one, we had 140 unique engineers log into our new Internal Developer Platform (IDP).
notes.interpretation: 採用曲線起點：首月 140 unique users。

notes.quote: In month two, that number dropped to 52.
notes.interpretation: 第二月腰斬到 52。

notes.quote: By month three—the week I was pulling the data—we had exactly 28 unique users.
notes.interpretation: 第三月剩 28，曲線終點。

notes.quote: Most of them were on my team (the platform team), checking if the IDP was still running.
notes.interpretation: 第三月 28 人大部分是平台團隊自己人。

notes.quote: A full 80% of the engineering org had tried our 'Spotify-like' developer experience, quietly decided it was worse than what they had before, and gone back to copy-pasting Dockerfiles from legacy repositories.
notes.interpretation: 八成流失，主動棄用，走回複製貼上 Dockerfile。

notes.quote: We had spent six months of dedicated engineering time building this. Four senior engineers.
notes.interpretation: 投入規模：六個月、四名資深工程師。

notes.quote: We had roughly 40 microservices, a growing EKS cluster, and a severe onboarding problem.
notes.interpretation: 背景規模：約 40 microservice、成長中的 EKS。

notes.quote: It took a new hire three weeks to get a service from their laptop to a staging environment. They had to know Terraform, Helm, GitHub Actions, and exactly which senior engineer to bribe in Slack to get an IAM role provisioned.
notes.interpretation: onboarding 痛點：新人三週、需懂多工具鏈。

notes.quote: We had custom plugins, a beautifully themed UI, and a mandate from the VP of Engineering.
notes.interpretation: 證偽 UI 假說：自訂 plugin＋主題化 UI＋VP mandate 三者齊全仍崩。

notes.quote: When a developer clicked 'Create New Service' in our shiny new UI, they thought they were getting a running container in Kubernetes. What they actually got was a GitHub repo with a `Hello World` Node app, a broken CI pipeline because the secret wasn't provisioned, and a Jira ticket automatically assigned to the DevOps queue asking for AWS permissions.
notes.interpretation: 期待 vs 實際的 before/after 素材。

notes.quote: We hadn't reduced cognitive load. We just put a React frontend over the exact same friction.
notes.interpretation: UI 假說排除後診斷。

notes.quote: To get your service to show up in the catalog, you had to write a `catalog-info.yaml` file.
notes.interpretation: YAML 維護稅起點。

notes.quote: When the team reorganized? Update the YAML across 12 repos. If you made a typo in the `owner` field, the YAML parser would silently fail, your service would vanish from the catalog, and you wouldn't know until the platform team pinged you two weeks later.
notes.interpretation: 維護稅明細＋靜默失敗模式。

notes.quote: I spend my day writing business logic. I am not going to spend 20 minutes debugging YAML whitespace just so my service has a nice icon on a dashboard I never look at.
notes.interpretation: 資深後端工程師原話。

notes.quote: We had shifted the burden of platform maintenance onto the users.
notes.interpretation: 作者評語：轉嫁維護負擔。

notes.quote: Backstage is a developer portal, not a developer platform...A portal is a pane of glass. It is a UI that aggregates information. A platform is the underlying engine that actually provisions infrastructure, manages state, and enforces policy.
notes.interpretation: 根源定義：portal vs platform。

notes.quote: We stood up the pane of glass, but we didn't build the engine behind it.
notes.interpretation: 根源一句話。

notes.quote: An interface over a broken process is just a shinier broken process.
notes.interpretation: 核心金句。

notes.quote: We realized that our engineers didn't want a UI. They lived in their terminals and their IDEs. They didn't want to click a button in a browser to create a service; they wanted to run a CLI command and have it *actually work*.
notes.interpretation: 工程師真正要的：CLI 不是 UI。

notes.quote: A developer platform should provide a 'paved road'—a path of least resistance that handles the heavy lifting (IAM, CI/CD, secret management, routing) automatically. If your platform requires developers to learn a new metadata schema, write extra YAML, or manage catalog state, it is a toll booth. Engineers will drive around it.
notes.interpretation: 規則一：paved road vs toll booth。

notes.quote: Humans drift; discovered state does not.
notes.interpretation: 規則三金句。

notes.quote: Our 'time to first deployment' dropped from three weeks to 12 minutes. That isn't because we built a beautiful dashboard. It's because we stopped trying to be Spotify, and started actually automating the miserable parts of our engineers' jobs.
notes.interpretation: 轉向後結果：三週→12分鐘。

notes.quote: If the lack of actual automation was the underlying disease, the metadata model was the symptom that drove engineers away.
notes.interpretation: 症狀 vs 病因區分。

notes.quote: We chose Backstage. It's open-source, extensible, and has a massive ecosystem.
notes.interpretation: 技術選型：Backstage。

notes.quote: Akhil
notes.interpretation: 文章作者 byline，經 re-fetch 於頁首確認。

notes.quote: July 1st, 2026
notes.interpretation: 文章發布日期，經 re-fetch 於頁面確認。
